fats.narration: 45.8 grams of fat. Saturated fat is 5.6 grams, a strong mark relative to the total fat. Omega 3 is only 212 milligrams, so this is not an omega 3-rich nut. For nuts, fat quality has to justify the calorie density. This is a mixed section: a clean saturated-fat mark, but weak omega 3.

carbs.narration: 27.6 grams of carbs. Fibre is 10.3 grams, helping digestion and slowing the absorption of the other carbs. Starch is only 1.4 grams, but nuts are not supposed to be starch-based energy foods. The glycemic index is 30, meaning these carbs raise blood glucose relatively slowly. For nuts, fibre and glycemic behaviour matter far more than starch.

proteins.narration: 21.1 grams of protein. Essential amino acids score 9 out of 9, meaning all 9 groups that the body cannot make clear the useful threshold. Bioavailability is 83%, so the protein is fairly usable after digestion. That is a strong protein result for a nut, even though fat quality and fibre still matter more.

vitamins.narration: Vitamin E is 14% daily value, providing some useful antioxidant support. Vitamin E helps protect cells from oxidative damage, but 14% is helpful rather than exceptional. For nuts, vitamin E is the headline vitamin, although it is not strong enough to carry the whole score here.

minerals.narration: Magnesium is 26% daily value, supporting energy production plus normal nerve and muscle function. Iron is 22% daily value, a softer mark than magnesium but still a useful contribution towards oxygen transport. For nuts, solid minerals help justify the dense calories.

pros.narration: The upsides first: portable and shelf-stable. They are easy to keep around and need no preparation. Roasted crunch makes a small serving satisfying. The texture and savoury flavour make a measured portion feel more substantial than many light packaged snacks. Still resembles the food it came from. Even roasted and salted, it remains closer to a whole food than most savoury snacks.

cons.narration: The drawbacks next: the salt adds a sodium tradeoff. This exact entry has 428 milligrams of sodium per 100 grams. Handfuls add up quickly. The dense, snackable format makes casual portions easy to overshoot. Nut allergy rules them out for some people. That is a hard practical limit, not a tiny nutritional downside.

closing.summary: Best bits are fibre, broad essential amino acid coverage, a low glycemic index, useful vitamin E and magnesium, plus portable whole-food convenience. Weak spots are modest omega 3, added sodium, portion creep, and allergy risk. Best for satisfying snacks or meal toppings in measured portions, where the protein and fibre make them more substantial. This is a strong nut held back slightly by the salted, easy-to-overeat format.
